edges.description: The p.Tyr375Cys allele and its murine equivalent produce ligand-independent receptor activation in experimental systems.

Human p.Tyr375Cys-associated BSS can include fusion of tracheal cartilage rings; the intervening developmental mechanism is unresolved and is not reproduced consistently in the corresponding mouse model.
The corresponding Y394C knock-in allele produces midfacial hypoplasia in mice. The experiment does not isolate suture fusion as its mediator.
Constitutive receptor activation is accompanied by increased p38 phosphorylation in mutant mouse epidermis and calvaria.
p38 contributes to the osteogenic phenotype, with increased ERK1/2 signaling also observed in skull tissue; p38 inhibition yields only limited suture improvement.
p38 inhibition reduces the mutant epidermal proliferation and differentiation abnormalities, supporting a functional contribution to epidermal hyperplasia.
Measures increased phosphorylation with the human disease allele.
edges.limitations: Heterologous overexpression in a tumor-derived rat cell line does not reproduce endogenous expression in human skin or cranial sutures.

nodes.description: Heterozygous FGFR2 variants cause the syndrome. The recurrent p.Tyr375Cys and p.Ser372Cys substitutions introduce cysteine residues in the juxtamembrane/transmembrane region. Functional studies demonstrate constitutive activation for human p.Tyr375Cys and the corresponding murine p.Tyr394Cys allele. A de novo p.Phe276Cys variant was classified as likely pathogenic in a 2026 prenatal case; its functional effect was not experimentally tested. A 63-nucleotide deletion has also been reported in a Beare-Stevenson-like presentation, so a cysteine-creating missense mechanism should not be imposed on every reported allele.

nodes.description: Halo-type external distraction osteogenesis to advance the severely hypoplastic midface, correcting proptosis and occlusion. The first successful Le Fort III distraction in BSS was reported in 2026 in a 5-year-old, achieving roughly 25 mm of distraction without major complications and sustained improvement at two years. Reported experience with the alternative monobloc advancement is more cautionary: in one BSS patient the temporal fossa was too narrow for the procedure to work well, and unrecognized micrognathia meant decannulation remained impossible despite the advancement. Prior shunt tubing and skull defects constrain the operative approach.

nodes.description: Vertical fusion of tracheal cartilage rings can produce a rigid sleeve along the trachea. Human BSS cases demonstrate this lesion, including progressive inward cartilage deformation in a child followed to age three. The resulting airway risks include impaired clearance and obstruction or tube malposition; tracheostomy does not remove the abnormal cartilage. No sleeve was found among the five newborn Fgfr2+/Y394C mice assessed by whole-mount morphology in a later study, limiting extrapolation from this model to the human airway phenotype.
